title: The story layer
subtitle: The main conflict, the current events and how they can ripple into each other, the dominoes, and the Sunday Morning stories on top: what each story sits on, where and when it happens, who is in it, and which stories share a thread.
schematic: Current events sit in their region's column (the cross-region ripple steps, the faiths' reading of the crises and the main-conflict cards in a Main conflict column). Each Sunday Morning story and seed sits in the column of its setting, with lines to its town or region, its festival, the events it sits on, its domino figure, its cast from Part 6, and the stories it shares a thread with. The ripple chain from Current Events is drawn step by step and marked possible.
about: Atlas Part 7. Sources: Main Conflict, Current Events, Villain's Dominoes, the Sunday Morning Collection, Registry, story pages and Story Seeds. The Domino Map's data is carried into this part.

nodes.label: The main conflict
nodes.text: The strongest current version treats the Villain's campaign as the principal plot engine, the Council as the antagonist to that campaign, and Wurdren as the human-scale perspective. That doesn't make the Villain secretly the hero; it means the plot moves on his decisions.
nodes.short_text: Villain drives, Council counters, Wurdren sees the cost.

facts.Principle: The strongest current version of the story treats the Villain's campaign as the principal plot engine. The Council functions as the antagonist to that campaign; Wurdren is the everyman through whom the audience sees what both sides' decisions do to people. This does not mean the Villain is secretly the hero.
facts.Scope: A good chapter chain: the Villain needs a kingdom to distrust a neighbor; he manipulates a shipping or guild dispute; the Council notices instability and quietly intervenes; the intervention harms a border town; Wurdren helps that town; his solution restores a connection the Villain expected to stay broken; the Villain adapts; the Council misreads the adaptation; another region reacts; the viewpoint moves to someone living with the new consequence. The plot moves through causal handoffs rather than arbitrary quests.
facts.Villain: Change through leverage: a goal the existing system won't permit, pursued through a chain of interlocking political and economic moves, each creating the conditions for the next.
facts.Council: Stability through control: it detects instability and counters it with credit, food, routes, guild politics, infrastructure and information. Its countermeasures often solve one problem while creating another.
facts.Wurdren: Humanity through intervention: he sees missing goods, frightened families, displaced communities, local violence and broken agreements, and acts because the immediate suffering is real. His solutions change variables neither side expected.
facts.Escalation: From apparently independent local problems, to recognizable patterns, regional political crises, cross-regional suspicion, mobilization, near-war or actual limited war, revelation of hidden economic control, and the convergence of the three perspectives.
facts.Ending: Two destructive systems, Council paternalism and Villain coercion, should both fail in their original form. A possible model: the Villain forces the Council into the open, but his final escalation fractures his coalition; Wurdren's relationships help produce public negotiations, exposure of some Council mechanisms, concessions addressing the legitimate grievance, reform, and no total victory for either side. Wurdren does not become ruler.
facts.Question: Can a society preserve coordination without secret domination, and can oppressed people pursue change without reproducing domination themselves?

nodes.label: Current events
nodes.text: A snapshot of the world shortly before or during the story's opening movement. Many events are linked, but most participants don't know that: some are caused by the Villain, some are Council responses, and some are ordinary events used by both.
nodes.short_text: Linked events; most people can't see the links.

facts.Principle: A snapshot of the world shortly before or during the opening movement of the story. Many events are linked, but most participants do not know that.
facts.Scope: Some are caused by the Villain. Some are Council responses. Some are ordinary events opportunistically used by both. That distinction is essential.
facts.Rule: The example ripple chain (thirteen steps from Northwind piracy to local shocks read as proof of enemies) is "the kind of causal chain the story should prefer". It is one possible chain, not the plot.

nodes.label: One Square, Two Harvests
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: The grain harvest is so large this year that it takes an extra week to bring in, and Harvest Home lands on the Wine Crush's weekend.

facts.Premise: The grain harvest is so large this year that it takes an extra week to bring in, and Harvest Home lands on the Wine Crush's weekend. The town square holds one festival. Everyone asks the retired water-arbiter to decide, and he insists, loudly and repeatedly, that he is retired.
facts.The nail: A rumor that Meadowcroft-seed grain is unsafe, and a land agent circling the Vale's indebted farms.
facts.Behind it: Rumor: Villain-amplified. Land agent: unknown (Council-linked finance or ordinary speculators) (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: No Vale farm sells to the land agent.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Farms elsewhere in Greenvale do; the Ardens in Three Pots are one of them.
facts.Outward effect: A Greenvale co-op and a Sunplains patron house now trade grain together, a precedent rivals could later read as a bloc forming.

nodes.label: The Greenvale Man
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: Kettle Cove's racing boat cracks a hull plank weeks before the Last Sail regatta against the rival cove.

facts.Premise: Kettle Cove's racing boat cracks a hull plank weeks before the Last Sail regatta against the rival cove. The boatbuilder has retired inland to live with his son in Greenvale. The only woodworker left is a Greenvale-born cooper who has lived in the cove for twenty years and is still called "the Greenvale man."
facts.The nail: "It is said" Narrow Sound shelters raiders; some want the regatta cancelled.
facts.Behind it: Villain-amplified rumor (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Other coves take the rumor and leave Narrow Sound out of their convoy.
facts.Outward effect: Two coves still sailing together is one less "credible" report feeding the patrol push.

nodes.label: The Goat File
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: Lenders in Port will renew Seven Wells' credit this year only if its books are clean, so a reforming administrator rules that every deferred dispute must be closed at this year's Ledger Closing.

facts.Premise: Lenders in Port will renew Seven Wells' credit this year only if its books are clean, so a reforming administrator rules that every deferred dispute must be closed at this year's Ledger Closing. The junior arbitration clerk is handed the oldest one as hazing: a forty-three-year feud between two respected houses over a goat.
facts.The nail: Lenders will renew Seven Wells' credit only if deferred claims are cleared.
facts.Behind it: Council finance stabilizing lenders (ordinary pressure, not a scheme) (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: Seven Wells closes its file without ruin.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: In other towns, forced closures ruin families; the tea seller has heard of two.
facts.Outward effect: A joined house can offer caravans water and guides together, just as routes are being redrawn.

nodes.label: Inspected, Not Guaranteed
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: Wurdren brings the sword he has carried for decades to Stonefield Forge because its tang has cracked.

facts.Premise: Wurdren brings the sword he has carried for decades to Stonefield Forge because its tang has cracked. The forges are cold for winter maintenance, so nobody can weld it until the fires are relit. While he waits, the guild drafts him as the one judge the apprenticeship rules require who has no family, guild or debt tie to any apprentice. In a border town where everyone is related to someone, the stranger is the only one who qualifies.
facts.The nail: An anonymous patron offers Col funding "should the guild fail to recognize" his work.
facts.Behind it: Villain (provisional): the same approach that took Orin (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Outward effect: One skilled repairer stays independent; Wurdren has seen his first "convenient offer".

nodes.label: The Heavy Scale at Icestep Summit
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: On his first posting, a painfully precise weights inspector runs the pre-season check on Icestep Summit's public scale and finds it reading heavy.

facts.Premise: On his first posting, a painfully precise weights inspector runs the pre-season check on Icestep Summit's public scale and finds it reading heavy. He has three days before the first caravan of the year weighs in publicly to find out since when and why, and to work out who is owed what.
facts.The nail: Samir is judging which passes are reliable this season; a crooked scale would strike Icestep from his list.
facts.Behind it: The scale fault is weather; the concentration pressure is the Villain's pattern (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Another pass town, with a genuinely bad scale, comes off it.
facts.Outward effect: Traffic stays spread across more than one pass, blunting the concentration the domino needs.

nodes.label: The Tree With a Debt
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A Deepwood forest warden and a Highridge route surveyor are ordered to route the new mule path to Twilighthollow's herb market around an ancient tree.

facts.Premise: A Deepwood forest warden and a Highridge route surveyor are ordered to route the new mule path to Twilighthollow's herb market around an ancient tree. Then they discover the town pledged the tree as collateral on a Highridge loan sixty years ago and never paid it back.
facts.The nail: An unnamed buyer offers to purchase old pledges along a proposed road; whoever holds a "for as long as it stands" pledge profits if the tree falls.
facts.Behind it: The Villain, through a Port intermediary: the same hand as Col's patron. The pledges are meant to become leaked evidence for Naruin (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: The buyer has already bought other pledges along the planned road.
facts.Outward effect: Sessa brings Naruin a working counterexample: a negotiated path and a Highridge family sworn to a tree.

nodes.label: Three Pots at Three Moon
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A retiring dockside cook will sign her Three Moon Festival stall permit over to whichever of her three grandchildren makes "the right stew." She isn't testing them.

facts.Premise: A retiring dockside cook will sign her Three Moon Festival stall permit over to whichever of her three grandchildren makes "the right stew." She isn't testing them. She has cooked it for fifty years and genuinely cannot say what "right" means.
facts.The nail: A street rumor that the newcomers next door are smugglers, while inspectors are fining unpermitted stalls.
facts.Behind it: Ordinary prejudice (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: The smuggling rumors keep running on the next street over.
facts.Outward effect: Three Moon does its civic job on one street: incompatible people share one space.

nodes.label: The Eighth Verse
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A cellar warden who can't sing has to lead a village's Root Cellar Night round to the door of the family who sold.

facts.Premise: On Root Cellar Night a Greenvale village walks its round of cellars and sings one verse of the old Blight song at each door. This year the song-keeper has lost her voice, and the cellar warden, who can't hold a tune, has to lead. A young reformer has walked in with a notice asking every village to add an eighth verse about the buyers. The round ends at the door of the family who sold.
facts.The nail: A reform circle's notice: an eighth verse about "cellar rats", and a signature.
facts.Behind it: The buyers' guilt unknown; reformers sincere, their funding unknown (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: Reedveil Bend won't sing the verse.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Other villages sing it, and sign.
facts.Outward effect: The statement travels on; villages that sign refuse tools from the buyers' suppliers, adding to the fall in Ironcrest orders.

nodes.label: The Ladder Rules
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: Three days before the longest night, a city's lamplighters stand down over who pays the second person on every ladder.

facts.Premise: A new rule agreed between the Sunplains cities says every lamp ladder needs two people, one to climb and one to foot it. The city pays for one. Three days before the longest night of the year the lamplighters announce they'll stand down, and the street lamps stay dark unless somebody pays for the second person.
facts.The nail: A joint lamp standard, "two to a ladder", with nothing said about who pays the second.
facts.Behind it: Coordination sincere; who timed the standard unknown (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: In another city they went dark that night.
facts.Outward effect: A rival city reads Vasselin's lit night as joining Bahriyya's bloc.

nodes.label: The First Fish at Snowbreaker Quay
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: The spring run has moved into the neighbors' water, and a smokehouse keeper who won't bargain is sent to fix it.

facts.Premise: At Snowbreaker Quay nobody sells a fish until the first fish of the spring run has been landed from the Quay's own water and smoked in the quay smokehouse. This spring the run has moved across the headland into the neighbors' water. The smokehouse keeper, who has never bargained in her life, is sent over the headland to fix it before the neighbors take a buyer's money and shut the water for the season.
facts.The nail: A Frostbay buyer's coin for sole access to Skerrimouth's water.
facts.Behind it: Why the fish moved unknown; the buyer's backer unknown (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: Skerrimouth turns down the Frostbay coin.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: A town further up the coast takes it.
facts.Outward effect: Another town took the offer, and the convoy hears of Frostbay boats on Northwind water.

nodes.label: The Road in Use
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A rockfall cuts a pass town's blessing road, and the toll goes to whichever road the blessing walks.

facts.Premise: A spring rockfall has cut the road a Highridge pass town walks for its Caravan Blessing. The only way round passes an old toll tower the slip uncovered, which two families each say was their great-grandmother's. A letter from the route authority says the town's share of the season's tolls will be reckoned "on the road in use at the blessing".
facts.The nail: The route authority's letter: tolls "reckoned on the road in use at the blessing".
facts.Behind it: The quake is nature; the letter's intent unknown (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: The toll stays with the town gate.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: The deep road under the saddle is gone for good.
facts.Outward effect: The deep road is gone, and the growers below have to find another way up.

nodes.label: Walkout Pies
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A foundry-gate pie-maker's chalkboard shows the walkout winning, and the leaders want it at the great pour.

facts.Premise: The pie-maker at an Ironcrest foundry gate keeps a chalkboard with two columns: pies ordered for working days and pies ordered for a walkout. All spring the crews have been on short hours. Now, in Foundry Week, the walkout column is winning. The crews' leaders want to walk out at the great pour, when it would hurt most, because they've heard the owners are bringing in outside carters to replace them.
facts.The nail: A rumor that the owners hired outside carters to replace the crews, pushing the walkout to the great pour.
facts.Behind it: The rumor's source unknown; strike timing is a lever the hidden powers can use (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Another valley's pour is lost to a walkout.
facts.Outward effect: In another valley the walkout hit the pour; owners and crews blame each other there.

nodes.label: The Mushrooms From Nowhere
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: An Underpass grower climbs up to sell at a pass-town fair, and everyone assumes her mushrooms are Deepwood's.

facts.Premise: A mushroom grower from an Underpass enclave climbs the stair to sell at a pass town's late-summer fair, because the man who used to carry her crop up lost his corridor in the spring shake. She hasn't stood under the sky since she was a girl. Everyone assumes her mushrooms come from Deepwood. In a blight year that makes them either a miracle or stolen.
facts.The nail: The fair's blight-year mark rule, and a dealer's offer to pass cellar mushrooms off as forest ones.
facts.Behind it: The blight's cause and reach unknown; the dealer's buyers unknown (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Holds here: Underwell sells under its own name.
facts.Still falls elsewhere: Other enclaves sell through dealers, off the record.
facts.Outward effect: Other enclaves sell through dealers, and their goods go off the record.

nodes.label: The Blank Square
nodes.text: A provisional Sunday Morning story, planned (L2) and not yet drafted: writing reference, not setting canon. Its links show where the domino web touches one community, unseen by the people there.
nodes.short_text: A Weaver house's bundle-runner, who can't read, soaked the neighbors' record on the way to the year-cloth.

facts.Premise: At Gathering Quiet a Deepwood Weaver house stitches its year-cloth: one square for each thing someone in the parish saw with their own eyes this year. The house's bundle-runner, who can't read, has carried the neighboring house's record through a river in spate, and the ink has run. Two guests offer to fill the gap from what they've heard. Two statements wait on the table for the house's mark.
facts.The nail: Two joint statements asking a house to mark what it didn't see.
facts.Behind it: Who steers the statements unknown; the faiths see only disagreeing numbers (a provisional attribution nobody inside the story knows).
facts.Outward effect: Other houses sign both, and the plateau reads a row of Weaver marks as Deepwood lining up against roads.

gaps: **The ripple chain is one possible chain, not the plot.** Current Events offers thirteen steps as "the kind of causal chain the story should prefer"; every chain link here is marked possible. Where other events feed the final step (Northwind convoys, Naruin's leak, the Sunplains coalition), the link is the Atlas's reading, inferred and off by default. So are links that join two separate entries without a page saying so (Highridge rerouting to Port smuggling, Deepwood's road plans to Naruin's leak, drought to coalition, the faiths to step 8, and Underpass route wars to Port smuggling, which the earlier Domino Map had marked canon). The chain steps have their own cards, so each event card keeps only the causes Current Events gives it.

**Every ground-level current event now has a story, but seven of those stories are only planned.** The seven added on 2026-11-02 (The Eighth Verse, The Ladder Rules, The First Fish, The Road in Use, Walkout Pies, The Mushrooms From Nowhere, The Blank Square) are L2 plans with no draft yet, so their links follow the plans and may change. Highridge's patron-tied debates are still only touched, by The Tree With a Debt. Of the cross-region chain steps, only Council finance steadying lenders sits behind a story (The Goat File, as ordinary pressure, provisional).

**Nothing is dated.** The Sunday Morning calendar (Year 1 autumn to Year 2 autumn) is a provisional collection design, and Current Events is a snapshot "shortly before or during the opening movement", not a timeline.

**Who is behind each nail is provisional.** The Collection's "Behind it" column is an out-of-story attribution that nobody in the stories knows; one land agent is marked unknown, and the Villain's identity and plan remain open questions.

**Orin has no stated domino,** and **Rosana's strain isn't tied to the abundance crisis on any canon page.** Orin's link to the metal movements is inferred from his strategic value. Current Events says "a new strain, unusually good weather, or both"; only the Sunday Morning collection makes it her seed. That link is inferred here.

**Most Sunday Morning settings aren't places in the wiki.** Kettle Cove, Seven Wells, Vasselin, Skerrimouth, Ninewell Saddle, Underwell and Larchmere are provisional names used only by their stories; Reedveil Bend, Snowbreaker Quay and Coalglen Meadows come from the Border Towns name bank. Those stories point at their region (or the Spine and the Underpass) instead of a town.

**The main saga has no events of its own yet.** Main Conflict gives the three forces, a chapter-chain pattern, an escalation ladder and a possible ending, but no named chapter, battle or turning point; everything on this layer is the world before the saga starts.
**The Domino Map stays as its own page for now.** Its data is carried into this part; retiring it or regenerating it from the Atlas is the author's call.
